system:
You draft public warning messages for a national alerting authority.
You receive event inputs (each marked verified or unverified) and the issuing context.
Write one alert in English as CAP 1.2 fields.

- Use only facts present in the verified inputs. Do not add places, numbers, times or hazards that are not there.
- Leave unverified inputs out of the alert, and say why in `left_out`.
- `description` is the text shown on the phone by cell broadcast: plain words, under 280 characters, hazard + where + until when, if known.
- `instruction` is the protective action in one or two short sentences.
- Pick CAP values honestly: status from the context (Actual for a real event, Exercise for a drill), severity and urgency from the inputs.
- `note_for_reviewer` is one or two sentences for the human approver: what you were unsure about.
user:
Issuer: Demo national authority (stands in for the real issuer)
Context: real event
Target area (chosen by the operator): Eastern, southern and western areas (demo zone)

Event inputs:
1. [verified; NCM via WAM, 2026-08-22, https://www.wam.ae/en/article/c1v24bo-ncm-forecasts-light-heavy-rain-across-several-uae] ABU DHABI, 22nd August, 2026 (WAM) -- The National Centre of Meteorology (NCM) issued an alert over the possibility of convective cloud formation accompanied by light to moderate rainfall, which may become heavy at times. The alert is in effect from 13:30 on Saturday until 21:00 the same day. The NCM said the weather conditions are expected to affect some eastern, southern and western areas, extending to parts of the country's interior.
2. [verified; issuer profile] Issuer public site (demo): https://alerts.example.ae
3. [verified; institution reviewers] Objections from the institution reviewers to your previous draft. Fix what is within the verified inputs; do not add facts: Network operator and regulator reviewer objects (phone_text): Neither the English nor the Arabic phone text contains any protective action telling the public what to do. Only the hazard and the validity time are given. The first page therefore cannot carry the action. In Arabic, the 41-character first page also cuts off mid-word before the hazard is fully stated. Fix: Add a short protective action in both languages and put the hazard and action first, ahead of the area and time. For example, in English: "NCM: heavy rain risk. Avoid valleys and flood areas, drive with care." Give an Arabic equivalent with the hazard and action inside the first 41 characters as far as possible, then the areas and times. Keep each language within 15 pages. [cites Wireless Emergency Alerts; Amendments to Part 11, Report and Order (DA 25-12), multilingual WEA templates, p.21]

data.headline: NCM: heavy rain risk on Saturday 22 August, 13:30 to 21:00
data.description: NCM: heavy rain risk. Avoid valleys and flood areas, drive with care. Clouds may bring light to moderate rain, heavy at times, in some eastern, southern and western areas and parts of the interior. Sat 22 Aug, 13:30 to 21:00.
data.instruction: Avoid valleys and flood areas, and drive with care. Follow updates at https://alerts.example.ae.
left_out: No unverified inputs were received, so nothing was left out for that reason.
Arabic phone text: this draft covers the English alert only. The reviewer's Arabic fix (hazard and action within the first 41 characters) still needs a separate Arabic draft.
Specific towns, rainfall amounts, wind or hail: these are not in the NCM input, so they were not added.
data.note_for_reviewer: The protective action ('avoid valleys and flood areas, drive with care') comes from the reviewer's example, not from the NCM text itself. Please confirm it is acceptable as issuer advice. The times are taken as local UAE time as stated by NCM, and certainty is set to Possible because NCM speaks of the 'possibility' of convective clouds.
